Report_ID: Binary occurrence of any nephrotic syndrome relapse by 12 months
Title: Eficacy of rituximab versus tacrolimus in dificult-to-treat steroid-sensitive nephrotic syndrome: an open-label pilot randomized controlled trial
Author: Mathew et al.
Comment: The paper does not print a separate 2×2 table for 'any relapse.' Nine patients with relapse in each analyzed arm are identified from the exhaustive Results categories (rituximab: 2 with one relapse plus 7 with two relapses; tacrolimus: 8 with one relapse plus 1 with frequent relapses), consistent with 11 of 20 in each arm remaining in sustained remission. Per the synthesis contract, totals shown here are all randomized participants (21 rituximab, 20 tacrolimus). However, one participant randomized to rituximab never received treatment and had no reported 12-month outcome; the paper's modified intention-to-treat efficacy analysis instead used 20 per arm. Thus, 9/21 versus 9/20 treats the participant with missing outcome as a non-event and is not a complete ITT outcome analysis. An available-case sensitivity analysis would use 9/20 versus 9/20. The paper did not report an RR for the binary any-relapse outcome, so no RR is entered.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Intravenous rituximab') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Design Type: Single-center open-label parallel-group pilot non-inferiority randomized controlled trial
domain: Pediatric nephrology; difficult-to-treat steroid-sensitive nephrotic syndrome
Participant type: Children aged 3–18 years with difficult-to-treat frequently relapsing or steroid-dependent steroid-sensitive nephrotic syndrome
Outcome measurement: Any relapse by 12 months; relapse was defined as recurrence of 3+/4+ proteinuria for at least 3 days
Outcome variable: Binary occurrence of any nephrotic syndrome relapse by 12 months

Report_ID: 1-year relapse-free survival as a proxy for binary relapse by 12 months
Title: Comparison of rituximab, cyclophosphamide, and tacrolimus as first steroid-sparing agents for complicated relapsing/steroid-dependent nephrotic syndrome in children: an evaluation of the health-related quality of life
Author: Li Wang, Jialiang Zhu, Mingyun Xia, Ran Hua, and Fang Deng
Comment: The paper reports relapse-free survival percentages, not verbatim counts of children with relapse. Under the anti-hallucination rule, relapse events were not reverse-calculated from 82.4% and 64.7%; therefore a trial-level risk ratio cannot be computed from this report as extracted. Table I's 0.5 (0.6) and 1.1 (0.9) are mean numbers of relapses, not numbers of participants with at least one relapse. Figure 1 also gives an adjusted HR of 2.346 (95% CI 0.586–9.389; p=0.228), but its contrast direction is not explicit and it is not the requested event-based RR; it was not entered. The exact assessment window is 1-year follow-up/1 year after treatment, but the paper does not explicitly state whether this is measured from randomization.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Rituximab') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False); unsupported or insufficient statistic type
Topic of Content: Steroid-sparing treatment for frequently relapsing/steroid-dependent nephrotic syndrome
Participant type: Children with frequently relapsing/steroid-dependent nephrotic syndrome not previously treated with steroid-sparing agents
Outcome measurement: Kaplan–Meier 1-year relapse-free survival; the paper does not explicitly define an individual relapse event in the supplied Methods/Results text
Outcome variable: 1-year relapse-free survival as a proxy for binary relapse by 12 months

Title: Efficacy of Rituximab vs Tacrolimus in Pediatric Corticosteroid-Dependent Nephrotic Syndrome: A Randomized Clinical Trial
Author: Basu et al.
Comment: The Results section presents the primary outcome as relapse-free survival (54/60 with rituximab and 38/60 with tacrolimus); the relapse-event counts used for the requested synthesis are the corresponding complements, 6/60 and 22/60, also specified in the supplied pre-identified effect. One patient with missing primary-endpoint information was imputed with the most common value in the respective group for the intention-to-treat analysis. The reported OR 5.21 (95% CI 1.93-14.07) concerns sustained remission, not relapse, so it was not entered as the relapse effect. The paper did not report an RR for relapse, and no RR was inserted into the reported-effect fields.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Rituximab') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Design Type: Prospective, single-center, open-label, 2-parallel-arm, phase 3 randomized clinical trial
Participant type: Children aged 3 to 16 years with corticosteroid-dependent nephrotic syndrome, in proteinuria remission, and without prior corticosteroid-sparing therapy
Recruitment source: Consecutive children attending the study center
Outcome measurement: Relapse was identified through urine dipstick and confirmed by urine protein-creatinine ratio. Relapse was defined by 3+ or 4+ albuminuria dipstick results for 3 consecutive early-morning specimens. Assessment window was 0 to 12 months after randomization.
